description: Assistant may write in its OWN card scope (#1189 enforce_assistant_scope, self-target arm)
note: The event kind mirrors 03_worker_scope so the two arms are directly comparable; what the vector pins is the scope decision, not that an assistant is a sensible source of task.completed (it is not dispatched, so the dispatcher's is_worker check drops it).

description: Assistant may write into its HOME wave's report card scope — the one card the Worker self-scope rule is loosened by (#1189)
Assistant writing into ANOTHER wave's report card is DENIED (the loosening is home-wave-scoped)
note: scope.wave/area deliberately claim the assistant's OWN home wave while scope.card points at a foreign wave's report card. Filling in $OTHER_WAVE/$OTHER_AREA instead would make the vector pass on the #232 wave cross-check alone, i.e. it would stay green even if the target rule stopped requiring the report card to live in the home wave.

description: Assistant emitting a Wave-scoped event is DENIED — this is what pins 'an assistant cannot advance the lifecycle or dispatch'
Assistant emitting an Area-scoped event is DENIED
Assistant emitting a System-scoped event is DENIED
Assistant writing into another WORKER card's scope (same wave) is DENIED — only self + home report card are reachable
Assistant forging scope.wave (own card id, foreign wave) is DENIED — the #232 anti-spoof check applies to the Assistant arm too
Assistant forging scope.area (own card, own home wave, foreign area) is DENIED — the #234 anti-spoof check applies to the Assistant arm too
note: scope.wave deliberately stays $HOME_WAVE so the wave cross-check passes and the area check is the only thing left standing. Without this vector the whole Assistant file stays green even if the arm stopped comparing scope.area against the home wave's persisted area.
